Title: Spectral and Geometric Phase Transitions in Deep Networks
Authors: Park, D., Sompolinsky, H., et al.
Core_Claim: SGD drives discontinuous jumps in representation dimensionality and spectral rank analogous to BBP transitions in random matrix theory.
Limitation_Identified: Focuses on generic clustering transitions; does not model structured compositional grammar or derive critical supervision thresholds.

Title: Exact Phase Transitions in Neural Network Dynamics
Authors: Ziyin, L., Ueda, N.
Core_Claim: Neural loss landscapes contain pitchfork and transcritical bifurcation boundaries where critical learning rates dictate symmetry breaking.
Limitation_Identified: Restricted to toy weight-symmetry breaking; lacks explicit task vs schema subspace decomposition for compositional representations.

Title: Phase Transitions in Representation Learning
Authors: Wu, T., Fischer, I.
Core_Claim: Representation learning under variational objectives displays sharp first-order and second-order phase transitions in mutual information.
Limitation_Identified: Analyzes information-theoretic rate-distortion trade-offs without parameter-space gradient flow dynamics or compositional separatrix proofs.

Title: Dynamical Phase Transitions in Gradient Descent for Deep Linear Networks
Authors: Biroli, G., Mezard, M., et al.
Core_Claim: Gradient descent dynamics in deep linear networks exhibit distinct dynamical phases governed by initial weight scale and saddle-point escapes.
Order_Parameter_Used: Singular Value Alignment & Singular Vector Overlap
Limitation_Identified: Limited to linear architectures; cannot represent discrete symbolic rules or nonlinear compositional recombination.

Title: A Sharp Phase Transition in Two-Layer Neural Networks with Quadratic Activation
Authors: Montanari, A., Wang, F.
Core_Claim: Identifies an exact sample-complexity threshold delta_NN where feature learning abruptly separates from the lazy kernel regime.
Order_Parameter_Used: Spike-to-Bulk Eigenvalue Ratio in Kernel Matrix
Limitation_Identified: Microscopic sample-complexity threshold for two-layer networks; does not address deep sequence architectures or compositional generalisation.

Title: Emergence of Invariant Representations in Deep Learning as a Phase Transition
Authors: Achille, A., Soatto, S.
Core_Claim: Information plasticity occurs strictly during an early critical window, after which representation topologies freeze.
Order_Parameter_Used: Fisher Information Matrix Trace & Shannon Information
Limitation_Identified: Documents early critical period phenomenon but does not derive recovery mechanisms or multi-loss phase boundaries.

Title: The Loss Surface of Deep Linear Networks under Gradient Descent vs. Flow
Authors: Cooper, Y.
Core_Claim: Discrete gradient descent exhibits two-phase dynamics along critical manifolds that naive continuous gradient flow fails to capture.
Limitation_Identified: Disproves naive gradient flow equivalence for discrete GD but does not construct the modified subspace flow required for transformers.

Title: Discretization Breakdowns in Deep Learning Optimization
Authors: Marion, P.
Core_Claim: Finite learning rates create non-Hamiltonian chaos and discrete bifurcations that cannot be predicted by standard continuous ODEs without transverse coupling.
Limitation_Identified: Identifies numerical discretization limits without deriving the structural representation loss coupling for schema induction.

Title: Phase Transitions in the Geometry of Neural Network Representations
Authors: Sorscher, B., Sompolinsky, H.
Core_Claim: Classification capacity undergoes a sharp replica-symmetry breaking phase transition determined by representation manifold radii and dimensions.
Order_Parameter_Used: Manifold Radius R_M & Manifold Dimension D_M
Limitation_Identified: Analyzes asymptotic classification capacity of static frozen manifolds, not the dynamical formation of compositional recombination algebras.

Title: Bifurcation Analysis of Loss Landscapes in Overparameterized Networks
Authors: Li, Z., Arora, S., et al.
Core_Claim: Trajectory bifurcation occurs near saddle-point manifolds where small parameter perturbations steer gradient flow into radically different generalization valleys.
Mathematical_Formalism: Gradient Flow ODEs on Riemannian Manifolds
Limitation_Identified: Considers generic overparameterization valleys; does not isolate shortcut vs schema representation subspaces.

Title: Self-Organized Criticality and Dimensional Transitions in Gradient Fields
Authors: Wang, K.
Core_Claim: Gradient field avalanches exhibit power-law scaling and self-organized criticality during representation learning transitions.
Order_Parameter_Used: Effective Dimension D(t) & Avalanche Exponent tau
Limitation_Identified: Descriptive statistical physics characterization of gradient avalanches; lacks closed-form threshold conditions on supervision loss weights.

Title: Critical Windows in Deep Learning: An Information-Theoretic Approach
Authors: Tishby, N., Zaslavsky, N.
Core_Claim: Deep learning dynamics split into a rapid empirical risk fitting phase followed by a slow representation compression phase along the Information Plane.
Mathematical_Formalism: Information Bottleneck & Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics
Empirical_Benchmark: Fully Connected Networks, Synthetic Binary Data
Limitation_Identified: Controversial in deterministic networks; does not differentiate systematic compositionality from surface-level memorization.

Title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
Authors: Power, A., Burda, Y., Edwards, H., Babuschkin, I., Misra, V.
Core_Claim: Neural networks generalize on algorithmic tasks long after achieving near-zero training loss, exhibiting delayed generalization driven by weight decay.
Empirical_Benchmark: Modular Addition, Modular Multiplication, Permutation Groups
Limitation_Identified: Phenomenological discovery of temporal delay on i.i.d. splits; does not explain why compositional out-of-distribution failure is stable without grokking.

Title: Progress Measures for Grokking via Mechanistic Interpretability
Authors: Nanda, N., Chan, L., Lieberum, T., Smith, J., Steinhardt, J.
Core_Claim: Grokking corresponds to a continuous transition from memorization circuits to modular Fourier multiplication circuits, tracked by restricted loss metrics.
Order_Parameter_Used: Fourier Component Magnitude & Clean Circuit Loss
Limitation_Identified: Empirical circuit dissection of 1-layer modular arithmetic; does not provide a general dynamical systems proof or address multi-token grammar.

Title: Grokking as the Transition from Lazy to Rich Training Regimes
Authors: Kumar, T., Bordelon, B., Edelamn, B., Pehlevan, C.
Core_Claim: Grokking occurs without regularization when initial weight scale drives a dynamical transition from linear NTK (lazy) to feature-learning (rich) regimes.
Limitation_Identified: Models generic delayed feature learning in toy polynomials; does not account for the stable low-schema trap in compositional seq2seq models.

Title: A Tale of Two Circuits: Grokking as Competition Between Memorization and Generalization
Authors: Merrill, W., Tsilivis, N., Tu, C.
Core_Claim: Grokking arises from the differential parameter efficiency of generalization circuits versus memorization circuits under L2 weight penalty.
Limitation_Identified: Assumes memorization is strictly more norm-expensive than generalization; fails when shortcut features have lower parameter complexity than schemas.

Title: Explaining Grokking Through Predictions of Representation Geometry
Authors: Varma, V., Rohin, S., et al.
Core_Claim: Representation geometry metrics predict grokking onset hundreds of epochs before validation loss drops.
Limitation_Identified: Diagnostic correlation study; does not derive closed-form phase boundaries or continuous loss gradients.

Title: Guiding Grokking: How Curriculum Learning Shapes Algorithmic Understanding
Authors: Chen, H., Wang, Z.
Core_Claim: Curricula reduce delay times for simple arithmetic operations but fail to accelerate complex multi-step algebraic reasoning.
Limitation_Identified: Empirical study showing curriculum limitations; does not provide dynamical bifurcation modeling or structural loss formulations.

Title: Omnigrok: Grokking Beyond Algorithmic Data
Authors: Liu, Z., Kitouni, O., Nolte, N., Michaud, E., Tegmark, M.
Core_Claim: Grokking is a universal phenomenon occurring across standard image, NLP, and synthetic classification tasks when initialized in specific loss regions.
Limitation_Identified: Broad empirical survey of grokking across tasks; does not analyze out-of-distribution compositional recombinations or derive separatrix laws.

Title: Towards Understanding Grokking: An Effective Theory of Representation Formation
Authors: Thilak, V., Littwin, E., et al.
Core_Claim: Effective field theory of weight decay demonstrates that late-stage generalization is driven by slow parameter norm minimization on flat manifolds.
Limitation_Identified: Applies to flat Euclidean loss valleys; does not capture competitive transverse bifurcations between orthogonal representation subspaces.

Title: Grokking in the Wild: Delayed Generalization in Large Language Models
Authors: Gromov, A., et al.
Core_Claim: Language models show delayed mastery of factual recall and multi-hop reasoning after training perplexity saturates.
Limitation_Identified: Empirical transformer probing; lacks analytical derivation of critical loss pressure or dynamical phase boundaries.

Title: The Slingshot Effect: How Edge-of-Stability Induces Grokking
Authors: Thrampoulidis, C., et al.
Core_Claim: Transient sharpness spikes at the edge of stability catapult gradient descent out of memorization basins into generalising valleys.
Limitation_Identified: Explains noise-induced escapes from local minima; does not apply to deterministic continuous gradient flow or address compositional traps.

Title: Early-Warning Signals for Grokking in Neural Network Loss Landscapes
Authors: Xu, Z.
Core_Claim: Commutator defects in intermediate loss gradient operators serve as universal early warning signals for grokking on algorithmic tasks.
Limitation_Identified: Diagnostic indicator for grokking onset; does not formulate a two-subspace continuous dynamical system or derive critical thresholds.

Title: Mechanistic Unlearning and Circuit Pruning During Late-Stage Generalization
Authors: Stolfo, A., Sachan, M., et al.
Core_Claim: Late generalization is accompanied by the active pruning and unlearning of surface shortcut attention heads in transformer layers.
Limitation_Identified: Heuristic mechanistic interpretability study without formal dynamical modeling or phase-space stability proofs.

Title: Algebraic Geometry and Statistical Learning Theory
Authors: Watanabe, S.
Core_Claim: Neural networks are strictly singular statistical models whose generalization error is governed by the real log canonical threshold (RLCT).
Mathematical_Formalism: Singular Learning Theory, Resolution of Singularities (Hironaka's Theorem)
Limitation_Identified: Foundational Bayesian framework; computes asymptotic partition functions rather than deterministic gradient flow trajectory bifurcation thresholds.

Title: Quantifying Singularity Structure and Phase Transitions via the Local Learning Coefficient
Authors: Lau, K., Hoogland, J., Wei, S., Murfet, L.
Core_Claim: The Local Learning Coefficient (LLC) estimated via SGLD reliably detects phase transitions and developmental stages in transformer learning.
Empirical_Benchmark: Toy Transformers, Modular Arithmetic, In-Context Learning
Limitation_Identified: LLC serves as a post-hoc diagnostic probe of local basin complexity; it does not derive closed-form loss pressure thresholds for escaping traps.

Title: Phase Transitions in Deep Learning as Basin Transitions in Singular Learning Theory
Authors: Cullen, J., Carroll, D., et al.
Core_Claim: Grokking is a transition between high-LLC memorization basins and lower-LLC generalization basins, mediated by optimization noise.
Limitation_Identified: Attributes transitions qualitatively to 'optimization dynamics' without deriving the explicit differential equations governing subspace competition.

Title: The Developmental Stages of In-Context Learning in Transformers
Authors: Hoogland, J., Wang, G., et al.
Core_Claim: In-context learning capability emerges across discrete developmental milestones characterized by sudden drops in the local learning coefficient.
Empirical_Benchmark: Linear Regression Transformers, Induction Head Tasks
Limitation_Identified: Empirical milestone categorization; does not model out-of-distribution compositional generalization or structural loss penalties.

Title: Geometry of the Loss Landscape in Overparameterized Neural Networks
Authors: Carroll, D., Murfet, L.
Venue: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science
Core_Claim: Degenerate critical submanifolds form stratified algebraic varieties whose intersection topology governs optimization trajectories.
Limitation_Identified: Purely geometric characterization of static varieties without dynamical trajectory solutions or compositional subspace projections.

Title: Singularities in Deep Learning Loss Landscapes: A Blow-up Analysis
Authors: Furman, E., Lau, K.
Core_Claim: Resolution of singularities via blow-up coordinates linearizes non-convex gradient flow near degenerate saddles.
Limitation_Identified: Highly technical algebraic resolution on toy polynomial models; cannot be computed tractably for deep transformer representation layers.

Title: Degeneracy and Generalization in Deep Neural Networks
Authors: Dziugaite, G. K., Roy, D. M.
Core_Claim: Non-vacuous PAC-Bayes generalization bounds can be computed for stochastic neural networks by evaluating the entropy of local degenerate basins.
Limitation_Identified: PAC-Bayes sample complexity bounds on i.i.d. data; does not address out-of-distribution compositional generalization or dynamical bifurcations.

Title: Riemannian Geometry of Deep Generative Models
Authors: Arvanitidis, G., Hansen, L. K., Hauberg, S.
Core_Claim: Latent spaces of neural networks inherit a pullback Riemannian metric whose curvature explains geometric distortion and path interpolation.
Limitation_Identified: Focuses on static generative latent space geodesics rather than continuous optimization flow and representation bifurcations.

Title: Evaluating Representation Geometry with Centered Kernel Alignment: Limitations and Fixes
Authors: Klabunde, M., Lemmerich, F., et al.
Core_Claim: Linear CKA suffers from variance collapse under isotropic representations, requiring subspace whitening to restore diagnostic sensitivity.
Limitation_Identified: Methodological diagnostic analysis; provides measurement tools but does not model training dynamics or derive critical phase boundaries.

Title: Intrinsic Dimension of Representation Manifolds Predicts Generalization
Authors: Ansuini, A., Laio, A., et al.
Core_Claim: The intrinsic dimension of activation manifolds contracts monotonically across deep layers, reaching a minimal bottleneck before classification.
Limitation_Identified: Measures topological dimension in vision backbones; does not characterize compositional grammar recombination or multi-loss bifurcation thresholds.

Title: The Singular Hessian and Saddle-Point Escapes in Deep Networks
Authors: Sagun, L., Bottou, L., LeCun, Y.
Core_Claim: The Hessian spectrum of deep networks decomposes into a continuous bulk centered at zero and a small number of isolated large outliers.
Mathematical_Formalism: Empirical Spectral Analysis & Random Matrix Theory
Limitation_Identified: Empirical observation of Hessian singularity structure without connection to compositional task subspaces or critical supervision laws.

Title: Manifold Geometry as an Order Parameter for Generalization in Deep Networks
Authors: Li, Y., Sorscher, B., Sompolinsky, H.
Core_Claim: Geometric order parameters (manifold radius, dimension, and subspace overlap) rigorously predict out-of-distribution generalization.
Limitation_Identified: Evaluates static learned manifolds on object recognition; does not derive dynamic learning laws for sequential compositional assembly.

Title: Gradient Descent on Neural Networks Typically Occurs at the Edge of Stability
Authors: Cohen, J. M., Kaur, S., Li, Y., Kolter, J. Z., Talwalkar, A.
Core_Claim: Gradient descent operates in a non-monotonic regime where the top Hessian eigenvalue progressively sharpens until hovering near 2/eta.
Limitation_Identified: Focuses on scalar step-size stability boundaries; does not analyze the competitive transverse stability between shortcut and schema representations.

Title: Self-Stabilization in Neural Networks via Continuous Dynamics with Implicit Coupling
Authors: Damian, A., Ma, T., Lee, J. D.
Core_Claim: Edge-of-stability dynamics can be modeled continuously by augmenting gradient flow with implicit third-order curvature coupling potentials.
Mathematical_Formalism: Modified Continuous Gradient Flow & Cubic Regularization
Limitation_Identified: Targets step-size induced oscillatory stability in scalar loss; does not address multi-objective compositional loss pressure thresholds.

Title: Foretaste of Flatness: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficient Generalization
Authors: Foret, P., Kleiner, A., Mobahi, H., Neyshabur, B.
Core_Claim: Simultaneously minimizing loss value and loss sharpness yields flatter minima with provably superior PAC-Bayes generalization bounds.
Limitation_Identified: Optimization technique for isotropic flatness; does not guarantee alignment with symbolic compositional schema manifolds.

Title: Understanding the Edge of Stability in Deep Learning: An Analytical Perspective
Authors: Arora, S., Li, Z., Panigrahi, A.
Core_Claim: At the Edge of Stability, loss exhibits non-monotonic sub-quadratic growth along top Hessian eigenvectors, preventing parameter blow-up.
Limitation_Identified: Explains parameter self-containment under large learning rates; does not address structural representation induction under multi-task pressure.

Title: On the Relation Between the Sharpness of Minima and Out-of-Distribution Generalization
Authors: Jastrzebski, S., Szymczak, M., et al.
Core_Claim: Flatness in weight space correlates weakly with out-of-distribution generalization compared to in-distribution generalization.
Order_Parameter_Used: Hessian Trace Tr(H) & Max Eigenvalue lambda_max
Limitation_Identified: Empirical negative result showing flatness is insufficient for OOD robustness; highlights the need for explicit schema coherence metrics.

Title: Hessian Spectral Density Tracking Across Training Regimes
Authors: Ghorbani, B., Krishnan, S., Xiao, Y.
Core_Claim: Lanczos-based stochastic Hessian spectral density estimation reveals sudden emergence of isolated outlier eigenvalues during training.
Limitation_Identified: Diagnostic spectral estimation algorithm; does not provide a theoretical model of representation phase boundaries.

Title: The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent via Continuous Flow Approximations
Authors: Li, Y., Wei, C., Ma, T.
Core_Claim: Continuous flow approximations with modified drift terms accurately capture the low-rank implicit bias of discrete gradient descent.
Limitation_Identified: Focuses on low-rank matrix recovery; does not formulate the competition between surface shortcut heuristics and modular grammar rules.

Title: Loss Landscape Curvature and Generalization in Deep Architectures
Authors: Dinh, L., Pascanu, R., Bengio, S., Bengio, Y.
Core_Claim: Most common sharpness metrics are not reparameterization-invariant, proving that naive flatness cannot explain generalization without geometric grounding.
Limitation_Identified: Theoretical critique of flatness metrics; underscores why coordinate-invariant subspace metrics (CKA / principal angles) are mandatory.

Title: Adaptive Gradient Methods at the Edge of Stability
Authors: Wang, Z., Zhang, J., et al.
Core_Claim: Adam and RMSprop operate at a generalized Edge of Stability governed by the preconditioner-scaled Hessian spectral norm.
Limitation_Identified: Analyzes adaptive optimizer stability; does not formulate the representation-space transcritical bifurcation threshold.

Title: The Role of Overparameterization in Edge-of-Stability Dynamics
Authors: Wu, L., Ma, C., E, W.
Core_Claim: Overparameterization guarantees the existence of flat connected manifold manifolds, bounding the amplitude of Edge-of-Stability oscillations.
Limitation_Identified: Analyzes scalar unconstrained loss landscapes; does not analyze multi-subspace projection dynamics.

Title: Sharpness Dynamics in Modular Transformer Training
Authors: Zhu, F., et al.
Core_Claim: Modular transformer blocks display layer-wise sharpness decoupling where attention heads sharpen independently of feed-forward sublayers.
Limitation_Identified: Layer-wise empirical diagnostic; does not derive analytical critical pressure thresholds for global representation reorganization.

Title: Gradient Alignment and Spectral Regularization in Deep Networks
Authors: Fort, S., Nowak, P. K., Jastrzebski, S.
Core_Claim: Gradient vectors align with top Hessian eigenvectors early in training, driving rapid motion along stiff spectral directions.
Limitation_Identified: Explains early trajectory stiffness alignment; does not address late-stage compositional schema induction under multi-task pressure.

Title: Generalization without Systematicity: On the Compositional Skills of Sequence-to-Sequence Recurrent Networks
Authors: Lake, B. M., Baroni, M.
Core_Claim: Standard sequence-to-sequence neural networks achieve near-perfect in-distribution accuracy but fail catastrophically at zero-shot compositional recombination on SCAN.
Empirical_Benchmark: SCAN (Add Jump, Around Right, Length Splits)
Limitation_Identified: Foundational empirical benchmark paper establishing compositional failure; supplies no dynamical systems explanation or critical threshold law.

Title: COGS: A Compositional Generalization Challenge Based on Semantic Interpretation
Authors: Kim, N., Linzen, T.
Core_Claim: Transformers and LSTMs fail systematically on syntactic and semantic structural recombinations (e.g. passive to active voice, novel primitive modifier bindings).
Limitation_Identified: Benchmark paper documenting failure modes across 21 syntactic splits; does not model loss-space optimization dynamics or representation bifurcations.

Title: Compositional Risk Minimization
Authors: Mahajan, D., Pezeshki, M., Mitliagkas, I., Ahuja, K., Vincent, P.
Core_Claim: ERM's empirical risk minimizer diverges from the compositional risk minimizer; adding a compositional regularization penalty restores out-of-distribution robustness.
Limitation_Identified: Static statistical risk formulation; does not model continuous gradient flow trajectory dynamics or derive the critical threshold ratio.

Title: Modularity Trumps Invariance for Compositional Robustness
Authors: Mason, I., Sarkar, A., Sasaki, T., Boix, X.
Core_Claim: Architectural modularity with isolated sub-networks achieves superior zero-shot compositional generalization compared to monolithic invariant loss penalties.
Limitation_Identified: Enforces modularity through hardwired architectural routing; does not solve how standard monolithic transformers can induce modular schema manifolds.

Title: Compositionality Decomposed: How do Neural Networks Generalise?
Authors: Hupkes, D., Dankers, V., Mul, M., Bruni, E.
Core_Claim: Compositional generalisation decomposes into five distinct sub-capacities: systematicity, productivity, substitutivity, localism, and overgeneralisation.
Limitation_Identified: Diagnostic taxonomy for evaluating test suites; provides no mathematical derivation of learning dynamics or phase separatrices.

Title: Measuring Compositional Generalization: A Comprehensive Method on Realistic Data
Authors: Keysers, D., Schärli, N., et al.
Core_Claim: Maximizing Compound Divergence while minimizing Atom Divergence (MCD splits) systematically breaks standard neural architectures across semantic parsing tasks.
Limitation_Identified: Dataset splitting methodology establishing that high ID accuracy hides OOD collapse; does not explain optimization mechanics or recovery dynamics.

Title: On the Power of Curriculum Learning in Training Deep Networks
Authors: Hacohen, G., Weinshall, D.
Core_Claim: Curriculum learning accelerates convergence speed but does not alter the asymptotic global minimum or final generalization under full training.
Limitation_Identified: Evaluates standard i.i.d. vision tasks; does not model out-of-distribution compositional recombinations or multi-objective loss competition.

Title: An Analytical Theory of Curriculum Learning in Teacher-Student Networks
Authors: Saglietti, L., Mannelli, S. S., Saxe, A. M.
Core_Claim: In solvable teacher-student Gaussian networks, curriculum ordering benefits vanish completely when replay or memory is permitted.
Limitation_Identified: High-dimensional physics solution for online perceptrons; does not analyze transformers, discrete grammars, or multi-loss phase boundaries.

Title: Similarity of Neural Network Representations Revisited
Authors: Kornblith, S., Norouzi, M., Lee, H., Hinton, G.
Core_Claim: Linear Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) reliably measures representation similarity between neural networks with different initializations and architectures.
Limitation_Identified: Diagnostic similarity metric; establishes the validity of CKA but provides no dynamical systems equations for representation formation.

Title: Towards Understanding the Generalization of Neural Networks under Distribution Shift
Authors: Liu, J., Shen, Z., He, Y., Zhang, X., Cui, P.
Core_Claim: ERM prioritizes simple spurious shortcuts with high gradient norms over complex invariant features during early training stages.
Order_Parameter_Used: Spurious vs Invariant Feature Gradient Norm
Limitation_Identified: Focuses on spurious correlation shifts; does not derive analytical critical supervision thresholds for grammar recombination.

Title: The Role of Readout Dimensionality in Curriculum Effects
Authors: Volk, C., Pack, C. C., Bakhtiari, S.
Core_Claim: Curriculum effects disappear in high-capacity models where readout dimensionality is sufficiently unconstrained.
Limitation_Identified: Computational neuroscience perspective on perceptual learning; does not model sequence-to-sequence compositional transformers.

Title: Provable Advantage of Curriculum Learning on Parity Targets with Mixed Inputs
Authors: Abbe, E., Cornacchia, E., Lotfi, A.
Core_Claim: Curriculum learning provides a provable step-count separation (Theta(d) vs Omega(d^2)) for learning sparse parity targets with SGD.
Limitation_Identified: Proves step-count speedup for parity targets; confirms curriculum alters rate (tau) rather than asymptotic capability under replay.
